newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals rise, led by palladium.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals rise, led by palladium.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures ended higher on Wednesday, buoyed by strong bullion prices and the weak yen, traders said.

All palladium futures hit their all-time highs. They surged by their daily limit of 22 yen per gram at the opening, and kept their gains for most of the day, traders said. Most-active benchmark February surged by its 22 yen limit to 597 yen at the close.
"Sentiment toward palladium remains bullish. It may take more time until Japan-Russia platinum group metal talks are held, given the political situation in Russia," a trader said.
Traders said buying interest in palladium by overseas investors remained strong. In palladium futures, trade house buying absorbed selling by private investors.
Private investors still held massive short-positions in TOCOM palladium, putting upward pressure on the market.
Gold futures ranged from 15 yen to 22 yen per gram higher, with most-active benchmark February ending up 16 yen at 1,381 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $353.40/70 per ounce at 0748 GMT, against $353.30/80 in New York on Tuesday.

In gold futures, private investors' profit-taking put a lid on further gains. "Gold's gains were in line with the strong performance of white metals. The upside at $355.00 could be tough to break on lingering concern over central bank sales," one trader said.
In platinum futures, active two-way trade was detected.
Platinum futures ranged from 15 yen to 34 yen per gram higher. Benchmark February was up 31 yen at 1,491 yen.
Benchmark February silver was up 1.9 yen per 10 grams at 206.4 yen.
